grounding.states: Short-term use at low-to-moderate doses (5 mg daily or less) for short periods appears safe and well tolerated
grounding.from: melatonin taken in low-to-moderate doses (e.g., 5 mg daily or less) for short periods appears safe and well-tolerated

grounding.states: Common side effects are minor and resolve once use stops; the most frequent are headache and somnolence (fatigue)

grounding.states: A later analysis found no significant association, per a summary; the question remains open

value.answer: For short stretches at low doses, 5 mg or less a day, studies found it appears safe and well tolerated. Common side effects are headache and grogginess, and they go away once you stop. Long-term safety isn't well established. A preliminary study presented at a heart association meeting linked 12+ months of use in people with insomnia to more heart failure, but it isn't peer-reviewed and can't prove cause. A later summary of a 2026 analysis found no significant link, so it's still open. Experts say don't use it long-term without a good reason. In the US it's sold as a supplement, so strength varies a lot. It may interact with blood thinners and antidepressants, so check with a doctor or pharmacist if you take either. I didn't find specific guidance on pregnancy.
